requirements.evidence: Every contract item is present. Queues.php declares all eight properties and fifteen methods; render passes accessQueue/accessGrants with collect() when null (Queues.php:212-223). Rename re-derives the slug: `slug: Str::slug($this->renameName)` (Queues.php:146). The toggle confirmation is a Bulma modal with queues_toggle_title/message, not wire:confirm (queues.blade.php:101-122). Serve.php: lastCalledTicketId is #[Locked], selectedQueueId defaults to the first callable queue, the exceptions map to notices, AuthorizationException is not caught, and the rate limiter is hit only on success (Serve.php:62-101). The waiting list orders by priority desc, issued_at, id with limit(30). The Members tabs use role="tablist" and setActiveTab whitelists the tab names. Both routes, both navbar links and every listed lang key exist in en and pt_BR.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through CreateQueue/UpdateQueue/SetQueueAccess/CallNextTicket, authorization uses policies, inputs use #[Validate], and all text comes from lang/*/ui.php. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] and docs/business-rules.md are updated. Deviations: role logic sits in the view inside a @php block with a fully qualified `\App\Models\UserRole::Owner` (queues.blade.php:150-153), and the navbar uses `@can('create', [\App\Models\Queue::class, ...])` inline. The four modals repeat the same Bulma modal-card markup instead of using a Blade component.

security.evidence: Every client id is resolved through the entity, e.g. `$this->entity->queues()->findOrFail($id)` and `$this->entity->memberships()->findOrFail($membershipId)`. accessQueue()/viewingQueue() use a scoped find, so a tampered id discloses nothing. callNext authorizes 'call', the mode is validated, and lastCalledTicketId is #[Locked]. Output is escaped with {{ }}. Small gaps: grantAccess/revokeAccess call no $this->authorize in the component and rely on SetQueueAccess authorizing internally (tested as forbidden). activeTab is client-writable and has no #[Validate]; render normalizes it.

tests.evidence: QueuesTest.php (414 lines) and ServeTest.php (370 lines) cover the happy paths, validation failures (empty name, duplicate slug, rename collision, unknown mode), foreign-id tampers that expect ModelNotFoundException, an employee calling every Queues action directly (`$refused('grantAccess', ...)`), an ungranted employee tampering selectedQueueId, the locked lastCalledTicketId, the rate limit, the navbar and translations. MembersTabsTest covers tabs and ignoring unknown tab names. The existing invite tests were adjusted to switch tabs rather than weakened, and UiTranslationKeysTest checks key parity between locales.

simplicity.evidence: Components are direct and reuse the existing actions. There is some redundancy: Members::render repeats the whitelist check already enforced in setActiveTab (`in_array($this->activeTab, self::TABS, true) ? ... : 'members'`). Serve::waitingTickets re-implements CallNextTicket's ordering and mode filter for display, which is acceptable as a read query. The modal markup is repeated four times.

readability.evidence: Methods are small, well named and follow the Members sibling pattern (row buttons, modals, `Untrusted client state` PHPDoc). Helpers are private (setAccess, viewingQueue, accessQueue, resetNested, firstMessage). Minor points: the @php role block in the access modal, and an employee-refusal test helper that needs a comment explaining that each attempt remounts the component.

scope.evidence: Every changed file serves the task: two components, two views, routes, navbar, the Members tabs, lang keys, docs/CHANGELOG and tests. The extra lang keys (serve_rate_limited, queues_save, etc.) support the requested UI. There are no unrelated refactors.

issues.explanation: grantAccess/revokeAccess do not call $this->authorize('manageAccess', $queue) in the component and rely only on SetQueueAccess authorizing internally, while the Livewire policy asks every public action to authorize server-side.
The role check (`\App\Models\UserRole::Owner/Admin`) and grant lookup sit in a @php block in the view; this logic belongs in the component or a policy check such as can('call', $accessQueue).
public string $activeTab is client-writable and has no #[Validate] or in: rule; render() normalizes it, so it is harmless, but this departs from the 'validate public properties' rule.
Four nearly identical Bulma modal-card blocks could share an anonymous Blade component, as the conventions suggest.
toggleActive($id) does not require $id to match viewingQueueId, so it works for any queue of the entity; this is authorized and scoped, but it bypasses the intended confirm-then-toggle flow.

review.summary: The change adds the Queues management page and the Serve panel, splits the Members page into tabs, and adds navbar links, translations in both locales, docs and extensive Pest tests (including foreign-id tamper, unauthorized-call and rate-limit cases). Every client id is resolved through the entity and all writes go through the domain actions, so the contract is met. Only minor points remain: grant/revoke rely on the action's authorization alone, role logic sits in the access-modal view, and modal markup is repeated, so I would approve with nits.
